verses.text: Listen, Israel! Today you’re crossing the Jordan to take land from nations bigger and stronger than you. Their cities are huge, with walls that reach the sky.
The people are big and tall. They’re descendants of the Anakim. You know who they are and have heard people say, “Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?”

Know this today: Yahweh your God is crossing ahead of you like a fire that devours everything. He’ll destroy them and bring them down before you. You’ll drive them out and wipe them out quickly, just as Yahweh told you.
After Yahweh your God drives them out ahead of you, don’t think, “Yahweh brought me into this land because I’m righteous.” It’s because of these nations’ wickedness that he’s driving them out.

You’re not getting their land because you’re righteous or your heart is upright. Yahweh your God is driving out these nations because of their wickedness and to keep the promise he swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Understand this: Yahweh your God isn’t giving you this good land because you’re righteous. You’re a stubborn people.
Remember how you made Yahweh your God angry in the wilderness, and don’t ever forget it. From the day you left Egypt until you got here, you’ve been rebelling against him.
You made Yahweh so angry at Horeb that he was ready to destroy you.
When I went up the mountain for the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant Yahweh made with you, I stayed there forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
Yahweh handed me the two stone tablets with writing from God’s own finger. They held every word Yahweh spoke to you from the middle of the fire on the mountain the day you all gathered.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, Yahweh gave me those two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Yahweh told me, “Get up and get down from here fast. The people you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves. They turned away from what I told them to do so quickly. They’ve cast a metal idol for themselves!”
Yahweh went on, “I’ve watched these people, and look how stubborn they are.
Leave me alone so I can destroy them and wipe their name from under the sky. I’ll make you into a bigger and stronger nation than they are.”
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was burning with fire. I carried the two covenant tablets in my hands.
I looked, and there it was: you’d sinned against Yahweh your God. You’d made yourselves a metal calf. You turned away so quickly from the way Yahweh told you to go.
I grabbed both tablets, threw them down, and smashed them right before your eyes.
I fell facedown before Yahweh again for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all your sin. You did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight and stirred up his anger.
I was afraid of how furious Yahweh was with you. He was ready to destroy you, but he listened to me that time too.
Yahweh was also angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, so I prayed for Aaron at the same time.
I took that calf you’d made, the thing you’d sinned with, and burned it. I crushed it and ground it down to fine dust, then threw the dust into the stream that ran down the mountain.
At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah, you made Yahweh angry again.
When Yahweh sent you from Kadesh Barnea and said, “Go up and take possession of the land I’ve given you,” you rebelled against Yahweh your God. You didn’t trust him or listen to what he said.
You’ve been rebelling against Yahweh since the day I met you.
So I stayed facedown before Yahweh those forty days and forty nights because he’d said he would destroy you.
I prayed to Yahweh, “Lord Yahweh, don’t destroy your people, your own inheritance. You rescued them by your greatness and brought them out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Look past these people’s stubbornness, wickedness, and sin.
Otherwise the people in the land you brought us out of will say, ‘Yahweh couldn’t bring them into the land he promised them. He hated them, so he took them out to kill them in the wilderness.’
They’re still your people and your inheritance. You brought them out with your great power and your outstretched arm.”
